label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report correctly identifies two XSS sinks where user input flows directly into HTML output via string concatenation. The first sink occurs at line 119 within the response.getWriter().println() call which includes the variable 'user', derived from user-controlled parameters. The second sink occurs at line 117 within another response.getWriter().println() call involving the 'rememberMe' cookie name. Both locations concatenate user-supplied strings directly into the HTTP response body without any sanitization or encoding, allowing malicious payloads to render in the browser.
